fields.description:
**As a field representative, I want to open Fidson FieldForce and be straight in using the same Microsoft login I already use for email** so that I'm not juggling another password and can start logging my day without friction.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Signing in uses my existing Fidson Microsoft 365 / Entra identity — no new username or password to create or remember.
- [ ] On my first sign-in, my name, role and territory are pulled from my company directory profile so I'm not asked to set them up.
- [ ] If IT disables my account in Entra, I lose access automatically — nothing left to clean up.
- [ ] If sign-in fails, I see a clear, plain-language message rather than a technical error.
- [ ] I stay signed in through a normal working day without being kicked out and made to log in again.

### Problem / job-to-be-done

Reps already sign into Microsoft 365 every day for email. A separate login for yet another tool is friction at the very start of the field day and a real barrier to adoption — exactly where we can least afford it. Fidson IT also needs joiners and leavers handled centrally, without manually managing a second set of accounts.

### Notes for prioritisation

* **Trust fit:** Core — central Entra control is what makes every downstream visit attributable to a known, current employee. Without it, nothing else can be trusted.
* Reads as low-effort/high-certainty: it's a standard OIDC SSO against an IdP Fidson already runs, and it's a stated proposal commitment ("one sign-in").

### Open questions / risks

* Confirm OIDC endpoints, tenant and the directory attributes that carry role/territory (Phase 0 / Phase 1).

**Persona:** Field Representative · **Epic:** FID-3 · **Slice 1 — The Core Visit Loop**

fields.description:
**As a field representative, I want my location and time captured automatically the moment I start a visit** so that my logged visits stand on their own and no one has to ask me to prove where I was.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When I start a visit, the app captures my GPS location and the time automatically — I don't have to do anything.
- [ ] I can see the captured location and confirm it before saving.
- [ ] If GPS isn't available where I am, I can still log the visit by choosing a location manually, and it's clearly marked as manual.
- [ ] Whether a check-in was GPS-verified or manual is recorded against the visit, so the difference is visible later.
- [ ] Location capture works even with no signal and survives sync (nothing is lost when I reconnect).

### Problem / job-to-be-done

Today leadership is asked to trust field reports with no practical way to verify them — the "trust but verify" problem. That's uncomfortable for managers, and for an honest rep it means genuine work is hard to evidence and easy to doubt. Capturing time and place automatically lets a logged visit speak for itself, with zero extra effort from the rep.

### Notes for prioritisation

* **Trust fit:** Core — this is the proposal's "a logged visit is a verified visit." It's the single feature that turns field activity from claimed into trustworthy.
* Sensitivity: reps may read geotagging as surveillance. The capability is core, but how it's introduced matters — framing and comms are handled in the Rollout epic (FID-9); design here should keep rep trust front of mind (e.g. visit-scoped capture, not continuous tracking).

### Open questions / risks

* Confirm acceptable GPS-accuracy threshold and how a low-accuracy or manual check-in is surfaced to managers.
* Decide visit-scoped capture vs any background location (recommend visit-scoped only).

**Persona:** Field Representative · **Epic:** FID-3 · **Slice 1 — The Core Visit Loop**

fields.description:
**As a field representative working territories with patchy or no network, I want to log a full visit offline and have it upload itself when I'm back in coverage** so that I never lose a record I worked for, and never end up with awkward duplicates.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] I can complete and save a visit while completely offline, and it's held safely on my phone.
- [ ] The app shows me how many of my entries are still waiting to upload, so I know nothing is stuck unseen.
- [ ] When I get signal back, my pending visits upload on their own — I don't have to remember to press anything.
- [ ] If my phone retries an upload, it never creates a second copy of the same visit on the server.
- [ ] Syncing keeps working even if I close and reopen the app, or signal drops in and out.

### Problem / job-to-be-done

Reps lose connectivity in the field constantly — it's the norm, not the exception. On today's spreadsheet-and-WhatsApp workflow that means scribbling it down to re-enter later (often delayed or lost), or sending the same thing twice and creating confusion. Field reality has to be designed in from the first release, not patched on later.

### Notes for prioritisation

* **Trust fit:** Core — this is the proposal's "works where the network does not." If reps can't rely on it offline, they won't trust it, and adoption stalls.
* Highest technical risk in the slice (offline queue + idempotent sync); de-risking it early in Slice 1 is deliberate. Re-stress-tested in Phase 7 (FID-8).

### Open questions / risks

* Confirm conflict-resolution rule (proposal states server timestamp wins; rep is notified of conflicts).
* Confirm how long unsynced data may sit on a device and any security expectation for data at rest on the phone (NDPC).

**Persona:** Field Representative · **Epic:** FID-3 · **Slice 1 — The Core Visit Loop**

fields.description:
**As a field representative, I want one quick place to record who I saw, where, when and a short note** so that my day lives in a single tidy record instead of being scattered across notebooks, spreadsheets and chats.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] In a few taps I can log a visit capturing the contact/HCP, the institution, the date and time (filled automatically), my location, and a short summary or next step.
- [ ] Only the essentials are required, so logging a visit between calls is genuinely fast.
- [ ] I can scroll back through my own visits for the day, newest first, to check what I've already logged.
- [ ] Every visit is tied to me as the signed-in rep and can't be mixed up with someone else's.
- [ ] If I miss something required, the app tells me clearly without making me start over.

### Problem / job-to-be-done

Right now activity is captured across spreadsheets and messaging apps, so there's no single, current picture of a rep's day and the same details get re-keyed more than once. Reps need fast capture in the field — a long form at the end of a call won't get filled in honestly or at all. This is the entry point that makes "one source of truth" real.

### Notes for prioritisation

* **Trust fit:** Core — it's the moment raw field work becomes a structured, reviewable record. Everything managers and AI see later is built on this.
* Deliberately lean for Pilot 1: the fuller detailing record (products detailed, samples, attendees, marketing content, competitor signals) is Slice 2 (FID-4). Expand only on the back of pilot feedback.

### Open questions / risks

* Confirm the minimum field set Fidson wants captured at pilot vs deferred to Slice 2.
* Confirm whether reps select an HCP from a managed list or can add a new contact on the spot (links to the pipeline work in Slice 2).

**Persona:** Field Representative · **Epic:** FID-3 · **Slice 1 — The Core Visit Loop**

fields.description:
**As a first-line manager (DM / FSM), I want to see my reps' visits soon after they sync** so that I have a live, trustworthy picture of what's happening in my territories without chasing anyone for a report.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] I can open a list of visits logged by the reps who report to me, newest first.
- [ ] Each visit shows me the rep, the contact/institution, the time, and whether the location was GPS-verified or entered manually.
- [ ] A rep's visit shows up for me shortly after their phone syncs — not days later.
- [ ] I only see my own team's visits, and reps can't see each other's (enforced server-side, not just hidden in the UI).
- [ ] I can filter by a specific rep and by date (e.g. just today) to answer a quick question fast.

### Problem / job-to-be-done

Today managers find out what happened after the fact — often days later, sometimes only at month-end — and confirming a visit took place is a manual, multi-week audit. A first-line manager needs to see that territories are actually being worked, right now, and be able to spot a quiet patch early, all without micromanaging or interrogating reps.

### Notes for prioritisation

* **Trust fit:** Core — this is the half of the loop that makes the rep's logging _worth something_ to Fidson. It turns "trust but verify" into "see it for yourself," and is the proposal's "oversight that informs rather than interferes."
* Closes the Slice 1 thread end-to-end: sign in → GPS check-in → offline visit log → manager sees it. This is the "smallest complete, verifiable thread."

### Open questions / risks

* This is the single-manager view needed for Pilot 1. Full hierarchy drill-down across ASM/FSM/RSM/DM/NSM and the coverage/compliance dashboards are Slice 3 (FID-5) — confirm that's the right line to hold.
* Confirm "shortly after sync" expectation (near-real-time vs a short polling delay) for the pilot.

**Persona:** First-line Manager (DM / FSM) · **Epic:** FID-3 · **Slice 1 — The Core Visit Loop**

fields.description:
**As a field representative, I want to plan my calls for the day and week against my assigned territory** so that I work my patch deliberately instead of from memory, and my manager can see the plan before the day starts.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] I can see the accounts and contacts in my assigned territory and build a planned itinerary for a day or week.
- [ ] I can reorder my planned calls and adjust the plan as the day changes.
- [ ] At the end of the day I can see planned vs actually visited, so I know what I missed.
- [ ] My plan is available offline and doesn't disappear if I lose signal.

### Problem / job-to-be-done

Today a rep's route and plan live in their head or a notebook. There's no shared view of who's meant to be covered when, so coverage gaps only show up after the fact, and a manager can't tell a well-planned day from an improvised one. Planning in the app turns intent into something visible and reviewable.

### Notes for prioritisation

* **Trust fit:** Supports — planned-vs-actual is what later makes coverage and compliance dashboards meaningful (Slice 3).
* Sequencing: this anchors the rep's day, so it sits first in Slice 2.

### Open questions / risks

* Confirm how territories and account assignments reach the app (manual, from a list, or synced) — links to discovery in Phase 0/1.

fields.description:
**As a field representative, I want to record exactly which products I detailed and how they landed** so that my call is captured properly and marketing and my manager can see what messages are working.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a visit I can record the product(s) I detailed, with the key message and the prescriber's response or objection.
- [ ] I can log more than one product against a single call.
- [ ] The detailing record attaches to the visit so it shows up in my day and in my manager's view.
- [ ] It works offline like the rest of the visit.

### Problem / job-to-be-done

Right now what was actually detailed, and how the prescriber reacted, mostly stays in the rep's head. Marketing can't see which messages resonate and which fall flat, and a manager coaching a rep has nothing concrete to work from. Capturing it turns each call into usable signal.

### Notes for prioritisation

* **Trust fit:** Supports — structured detailing data is the raw material the AI insights slice (FID-7) later turns into next-best-action and message effectiveness.

### Open questions / risks

* Confirm the product list source and how often it changes (links to ERP/marketing data in Slice 4).
* Confirm which response/objection options Fidson wants as quick-pick vs free text.

**Persona:** Field Representative · **Epic:** FID-4 · **Slice 2 — The Complete Field Call**

fields.description:
**As a field representative, I want to log the samples I hand out on a call** so that there's a clean record of the stock I'm accountable for and we can stand behind it in any review.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a visit I can record the sample product(s) and quantity given to that HCP.
- [ ] I can see a running tally of samples I've issued over a period.
- [ ] Each sample entry ties to the visit and the HCP who received it.
- [ ] It works offline and syncs without duplication.

### Problem / job-to-be-done

Sample accountability is handled on paper or not at all, so reconciling what was issued against what was distributed is painful — and in a regulated industry that's a real exposure. A rep wants their record to be clean and defensible, not a liability at audit time.

### Notes for prioritisation

* **Trust fit:** Core (compliance) — sample tracking feeds the always-on audit trail the proposal promises for NAFDAC and internal record-keeping.

### Open questions / risks

* Confirm whether sample stock-on-hand per rep needs to be tracked (links to ERP in Slice 4) or just issuance at pilot.
* Confirm any NAFDAC-specific fields required on a sample record.

fields.summary: Rep captures a new contact on the spot, with consent

fields.description:
**As a field representative, when I meet someone new in the field, I want to capture their details on the spot — with their consent** so that a promising contact becomes a company asset instead of a name lost in my notebook, and any follow-up rests on a clear, lawful basis.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] During or right after a call I can add a new contact (prescriber, pharmacist, procurement lead) with a few key fields.
- [ ] The new contact enters the customer pipeline at the first stage automatically.
- [ ] I record the contact's consent at capture, timestamped, so it's auditable later.
- [ ] If consent isn't given, the contact is still captured but flagged as not-yet-consented, and outreach to them is held back.
- [ ] The app warns me if the contact looks like a duplicate of someone already in the system.
- [ ] It all works offline.

### Problem / job-to-be-done

New contacts currently live in reps' heads and notebooks, so when a rep moves on, the relationship is lost to Fidson. And outreach without a recorded consent basis is a compliance risk under the NDPC. Capturing the contact and the consent in the same moment turns a chance meeting into a durable, lawful asset.

### Notes for prioritisation

* **Trust fit:** Core (compliance) — this is the proposal's "consent on record": every contact carries its own timestamped, auditable consent record.
* This is the front door of the "from first meeting to customer" pipeline; progression is handled in the next story.

### Open questions / risks

* Confirm the lawful basis and exact consent wording Fidson wants captured (NDPC).
* Confirm the minimum contact fields required at capture vs enriched later.

**Persona:** Field Representative · **Epic:** FID-4 · **Slice 2 — The Complete Field Call**

fields.summary: Rep moves a contact through the pipeline to customer

fields.description:
**As a field representative, I want to move a contact along a clear funnel as the relationship develops** so that I can see real progress from first meeting to customer, and that progress belongs to Fidson rather than just to me.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] I can see my pipeline of contacts grouped by stage (e.g. new → engaged → qualified → customer).
- [ ] I can move a contact to the next stage and add a note on why.
- [ ] I can enrich a contact's details over time as I learn more.
- [ ] My manager can see my team's pipeline (read access tied to the hierarchy work in Slice 3).
- [ ] Stage changes are timestamped so the history of the relationship is visible.

### Problem / job-to-be-done

Relationships that live only in a rep's head don't compound and don't survive the rep changing territory or leaving. A visible funnel makes the developing relationship a managed asset — the proposal's "relationships that once lived in a rep's head become a company asset that compounds." Reps also benefit: their pipeline becomes evidence of work in progress, not just closed visits.

### Notes for prioritisation

* **Trust fit:** Supports — turns scattered contacts into a measurable, reviewable pipeline.
* Depends on contact capture (FID-20).

### Open questions / risks

* Confirm Fidson's actual funnel stages and what "customer" means in their commercial language.
* Confirm whether converting a contact to a customer should create/link a record in Business Central (Slice 4).

**Persona:** Field Representative · **Epic:** FID-4 · **Slice 2 — The Complete Field Call**

fields.description:
**As a field representative, I want to set a next step and a reminder on a visit** so that I follow up at the right moment and nothing important slips through the cracks.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a visit I can record a next step and a due date.
- [ ] My open next steps surface as reminders, and show up against my day plan.
- [ ] I can mark a reminder done or snooze it to another day.
- [ ] Reminders work offline and stay accurate after sync.

### Problem / job-to-be-done

A good call is only worth as much as the follow-up. Today follow-ups depend on a rep's memory or a scribbled note, so commitments to prescribers quietly get missed. Tying a next step to the visit means the system carries the follow-up, not the rep's memory.

### Notes for prioritisation

* **Trust fit:** Supports — reliable follow-through is part of what makes the field operation feel professional to customers.

### Open questions / risks

* Confirm whether managers should see/assign next steps to reps, or whether this stays rep-private at pilot.

**Persona:** Field Representative · **Epic:** FID-4 · **Slice 2 — The Complete Field Call**

fields.description:
**As a field representative, I want approved, current marketing materials available on my phone** so that I detail with the right message and never risk showing something outdated or off-label.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] I can browse and show approved marketing content for the products I detail.
- [ ] Only current, approved versions are available — superseded material drops off.
- [ ] Content is available offline so I can show it without signal.
- [ ] I can optionally note which content I showed on a call.

### Problem / job-to-be-done

Reps often carry their own copies of detailing materials, which means versions drift and out-of-date or unapproved content can end up in front of a prescriber — a genuine regulatory and brand risk. Serving approved content through the app keeps every rep on-message and on-label, and gives marketing control of what's in the field.

### Notes for prioritisation

* **Trust fit:** Core (compliance) — controlled, approved-only content reduces regulatory exposure and protects the brand.

### Open questions / risks

* Confirm who publishes/approves content and how often it changes (likely a marketing/admin role to be defined).
* Confirm content types and sizes for offline caching (PDF, images, video?).

**Persona:** Field Representative · **Epic:** FID-4 · **Slice 2 — The Complete Field Call**

fields.description:
**As a field representative, I want to quickly note competitor activity I see in the field** so that marketing and leadership get an early, ground-level read on the market without me writing a report.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a call I can log a competitor signal (competitor/brand, what I saw, and where/which HCP) in a few taps.
- [ ] Capture is lightweight enough that I'll actually do it in the moment.
- [ ] The signal ties to the visit and location.
- [ ] It works offline.

### Problem / job-to-be-done

Reps are Fidson's eyes in the market and constantly see competitor pricing, promotions and detailing — but that intelligence evaporates because there's nowhere quick to put it. Capturing it as a light field entry turns hundreds of reps into an early-warning network for marketing and leadership.

### Notes for prioritisation

* **Trust fit:** Neutral (commercial value rather than trust infrastructure) — but high strategic value as aggregated market signal.
* Aggregation and pattern-spotting across signals is where the AI insights slice (FID-7) adds leverage.

### Open questions / risks

* Confirm the competitor list / brands Fidson wants to track, and whether free-text capture is allowed alongside.

**Persona:** Field Representative · **Epic:** FID-4 · **Slice 2 — The Complete Field Call**

fields.description:
**As a sales manager at any level of the Fidson hierarchy (DM, FSM, ASM, RSM, NSM), I want to see exactly the field data for the people beneath me — and nothing I shouldn't** so that I can supervise my part of the organisation with confidence that the boundaries are right.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] My access reflects my place in the hierarchy: a Regional Manager sees the Area Managers below them and everyone beneath those; an Area Manager sees only their reps.
- [ ] I cannot see peers' teams or data above my level.
- [ ] Access is enforced at the data layer, not just hidden in the screen, so it holds even via direct API access.
- [ ] When the reporting line changes, what I can see updates accordingly.

### Problem / job-to-be-done

Fidson's field force runs through a real management chain (ASM/FSM/RSM/DM/NSM). Oversight is only trustworthy if each manager sees precisely their span — no blind spots below, no overreach above. Getting this right is the backbone that every dashboard, approval and report in this slice depends on.

### Notes for prioritisation

* **Trust fit:** Core — correct, data-layer-enforced visibility is the foundation of the entire management thread. Build it first in Slice 3.
* Technical note: recursive hierarchy + row-level security; flagged in the engineer interview guide as a key design question.

### Open questions / risks

* Confirm the definitive Fidson hierarchy and titles, and how matrix/temporary reporting (e.g. acting managers) should be handled.
* Confirm source of truth for reporting lines (directory vs in-app).

**Persona:** Sales Management (DM/FSM/ASM/RSM/NSM) · **Epic:** FID-5 · **Slice 3 — Oversight, Approvals & Reporting**

fields.description:
**As a sales manager, I want a dashboard of coverage and compliance across my teams that I can drill from the top down to an individual rep** so that I can see at a glance that territories are being worked, and zoom in only when something needs my attention.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] I see coverage and compliance summarised for my whole span, then can drill national → regional → area → rep.
- [ ] Coverage shows planned vs actual visits and where territories are under-worked.
- [ ] Compliance surfaces things like GPS-verified vs manual check-ins and consent completeness.
- [ ] The view is current (reflects recently synced activity), not a month-old export.
